en.title: The best and biggest games of September
en.description: Silent Hill: Townfall, Control Resonant, and Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave
en.fullContent:
Silent Hill: Townfall, Control Resonant, and Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave
                
                    
                    Konami, Remedy Entertainment, Nintendo
                    
                
                hide caption

September's more packed than any month in recent memory, as publishers rush to debut games before Grand Theft Auto 6's November 19th release. Ahead of that seismic gaming event, check out these five titles ranging from action to horror to fantasy.

I've played countless video games that put you in the hands of a swordsman cutting down foes. So it's a shock to me too to say that Onimusha: Way of the Sword is the best-feeling action game of them all. Never has a dodge, parry, or frame-perfect counter felt so dang good.

Nor have they looked so cool. Capcom developers told Game Informer that their biggest goal was to take the action of cutscenes from previous Onimusha games and turn it into playable gameplay. Way of the Sword achieves that with fluid animation that makes every encounter feel like a choreographed martial arts movie.

Dodge, parry and counter your way through Onimusha.
                
                    
                    Capcom
                    
                
                hide caption

It's not all great. Re-used bosses and a half-baked open world design lead to pacing issues and a kind of unnecessary fatigue. Which is weird. Capcom usually puts out tightly paced, lean games. It's a blight on something otherwise so polished.

en.title: The Best Video Game Movies and TV Shows
en.description: Is the era of the bad video game adaptation finally over? There have been enough great movies and TV shows over the past few years to suggest that ...
en.fullContent:
Is the era of the bad video game adaptation finally over? There have been enough great movies and TV shows over the past few years to suggest that the curse has been lifted. Gone are the days of mediocre Tomb Raider films being as good as we had it and live-action Mario movies haunting our collective nightmares. For clarity, this is separate from our older Best Video Game Movies list, which you can check out here if you so wish. From Netflix animations to live-action survival horrors, here are what we think are the 10 best video game movies and TV shows.

Veteran British actor Bill Nighy voicing the equally legendary Mewtwo is just one of the reasons why Pokemon Detective Pikachu is an enjoyable time. Tim (Justice Smith) and Lucy’s (Kathryn Newton) adventure to find the former’s missing father unravels a mystery worthy of this world’s greatest detective. Voiced with charm by Ryan Reynolds, Detective Pikachu is just the pocket monster for the job, as he leads us through Ryme City and a view into the world of Pokemon as we’ve never seen before.

Few games have as flashy action as Capcom’s Devil May Cry does, so it’s no surprise that the Netflix series based on the games has some of the sharpest animation seen on the platform. Demon hunter Dante is tasked with keeping the Earth safe from the Hellish threats lurking in a neighboring realm, and stylishly unloads thousands of bullets doing so. Season 1 builds up to a truly bonkers finale of the sort the source material demands, as Hoon Lee’s villainous White Rabbit steals the show, while 2026’s second season shines the spotlight on the enigmatic Vergil. It’s never subtle, but certainly entertaining, even if it’s not the best Netflix adaptation on our list.

If at the turn of the century you’d have told us that Jim Carrey and Keanu Reeves were starring in a movie together, we would have been very excited. If you’d then told us that they’d be playing Dr Robotnik and Shadow the Hedgehog, we’d have been confused, but likely still excited. The fact that the Sonic films are seemingly the only ones that can coax Carrey out of retirement will always be confusing, but we’re not complaining too much when the third of this trilogy has given us some of his best work in a long time. Sonic the Hedgehog 3 is the best of a series that only seems to be getting better over time, as they up the stakes, absurdity, and quality of Ben Schwartz’s loveable blue blur’s adventures with each outing.

Whether they’re good adaptations or not, there’s no denying that video game movies are seeing unprecedented success at the box office. Resident Evil has smashed all expectations, but it’s the family-friendly films that have been raking in billions.

One thing that can’t be denied about The Super Mario Bros. Movie is how good it looks. A vibrant, colourful translation of the Mushroom Kingdom and beyond from the masters of digital animation at Illumination, there’s a reason why so many younger viewers (and older ones, like us) can’t peel our eyes away from it. A quickfire tour through some of the series’ greatest hits — from musical cues of the original platformer to the hectic action of Mario Kart — the film served as a satisfying reintroduction to the big screen for gaming’s greatest pair of plumbers.

en.title: Try the latest Game Trial, Prince of Persia The Lost Crown
en.description: From Sept. 24 at 10 a.m. PT to Sept. 30 at 11:59 p.m. PT, Nintendo Switch Online members* can download and try the full Prince of Persia The Lost C...
en.fullContent:
From Sept. 24 at 10 a.m. PT to Sept. 30 at 11:59 p.m. PT, Nintendo Switch Online members* can download and try the full Prince of Persia The Lost Crowngame for the Nintendo Switch™ system at no additional cost.

Dash into a stylish and thrilling action-adventure platformer set in a mythological Persian world where the boundaries of time and space are yours to manipulate. Play as Sargon and evolve from sword-wielding prodigy to extraordinary legend as you master acrobatic combat and unlock Time Powers and unique super abilities.

If you decide to purchase the game during or after this offer, you’ll keep all save data, so you won’t have to worry about losing your progress. As an added bonus, for a limited time you can purchase the digital version of Prince of Persia The Lost Crown for 70% off at Nintendo eShop and Nintendo Store! This sale ends Oct. 7 at 11:59 p.m. PT.

Stay tuned for more Game Trials you can play on the Nintendo Switch™ 2 and Nintendo Switch systems.

Nintendo Switch Online members can complete a mission and earn 100 Platinum Points** just by trying out this Game Trial!

Game Trials like this are a perk for Nintendo Switch Online members, along with other benefits like:
